samples.question: The picture shows thick black walls drawn on white paper, laid out on a square lattice so that they enclose a compound of rooms. The black walls are solid and cannot be walked through. Wherever the lattice carries no ink at all, the way is open. Three places in the walls are open doorways, each painted as one coloured bar filling the gap it stands in - one amber, one magenta and one azure - and you can walk straight through a coloured bar. As things are drawn, every part of the white floor inside the compound can be walked out to the white paper outside it. Now suppose one single doorway were bricked up, so that its coloured bar became solid wall while the other two doorways stayed open. Exactly one of the three colours has this property: bricking up that one doorway would leave some part of the white floor completely shut in, with no walking path out to the paper outside the compound. Bricking up either of the other two would leave every part of the floor still able to get out. Which doorway is it - amber, magenta or azure?
